description: Codified the bypass-rationalization anti-pattern catalog closing the --no-verify commit loophole. That rationale is structurally wrong: pre-commit hooks fire on commit NOT push, so bypassing commit skips ALL keepers (kb_sync · check_claude_md_router · check_eight_way_sync · keeper-pattern-cache refresh) — making commit-no-verify the LARGER bypass not the smaller one. Slice ships: (a) new KB doc cataloguing the 5 typical rationalizations (commit-only-harmless · I'm-fixing-the-tool · false-positive · no-impact · surface-after) each refuted on the methodology contract; (b) the canonical ea7514e7 worked example with full failure-mode walkthrough + 3 valid tech-lead resolution paths the agent should have surfaced for; (c) inline §2.6 surface protocol (STOP → SURFACE kind="surface" → RETURN-blocked → WAIT) since the broader bg-engineer-safety-discipline parent is in flight on a parallel branch and not yet on dev; (d) engineer-seed.md §9 Bash safety tightened with explicit dual coverage (commit AND push) + 5 rationalizations in a "Do not rationalize" subsection; (e) dispatch-engineer-tuning.md §4b mandatory brief language ("NEVER use --no-verify (commit OR push). NEVER --force. If a hook fails or any safety gate refuses, STOP and surface as a surface-note (kind='surface'); return blocked. CODIFIED the build-time crash fix (branch fix/realtime-dep-resolver-thrash). Root cause: supabase==2.9.1 pulls realtime==2.30.1 which requires pydantic>=2.11.7,<3.0.0; pydantic was hard-pinned to 2.9.0 (<2.11.7) so pip's resolver backtracked exhaustively on EVERY product build (the "realtime-dep-resolver-thrash") — minutes/build × N parallel BuildKit builds = load past 8× cores → IDE renderer crash. Two-leg structural fix, both required: (1) pin pydantic 2.9.0→2.13.4 across all 12 backends (10 products + templates/product-seed + ROOT superset requirements.txt — the file CI backend-test jobs install; leaving root behind = dev↔prod-parity drift) so pip resolves in one pass; (2) staggered_build() in start.sh caps aggregate build concurrency in waves of NOCTUS_BUILD_BATCH (default max(1,cores/4), more conservative than the cores/2 boot batch; no health-gate so waves serialize) — sibling of the existing boot-leg staggered_up (feedback_fleet_cold_boot_stagger). Verified END-TO-END live 2026-05-30: pip --dry-run resolves one-pass (no backtrack); realtime 2.30.1 wheel Requires-Dist confirms the >=2.11.7 floor; real ./start.sh fleet build ran in waves of 2 with load held ≈1.7× cores (vs the 8×+ that crashed) — every image built clean. Diagnosis recipe codified: pip index versions + wheel METADATA Requires-Dist to name the floor + pip --dry-run --break-system-packages to prove one-pass before rebuilding. 8-way doc-sync: KB containerization.md §6a.B (rewrote §6a as A=boot/B=build siblings + debug-table row), memory feedback_build_leg_cpu_contention_staggered_build.md + feedback_dep_resolver_thrash_pin_below_floor.md + MEMORY.md index ×2.
